newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Datang sees 1996 profit at 920 mln yuan - sources.
newsitem.headline: Datang sees 1996 profit at 920 mln yuan - sources.

text.p: China's Beijing Datang Power Generation Co Ltd estimates its profit to be about 920 million yuan for the year ended in December 1996, up from 829 million yuan in 1995, market sources said in Hong Kong on Wednesday.

"The company estimates its 1996 profit at 920 million yuan and it further forecasts its profit to rise to 1,098 million yuan for the year ending in December 1997," said one analyst after attending a company presentation on Wednesday.
Datang recorded a profit of 798 million yuan in 1994 and 740 million yuan in 1993, sources said.
Datang, a subsidiary of North China Power Group Co, operates coal-fire electric power plants which supply electricity to Beijing and other industrial cities in northern China.

The company is expected to raise US$380 million by issuing 1.244 billion H-shares, representing 25 percent of its share capital, in a primary listing in Hong Kong and a secondary listing in London, the sources said.
The shares are expected to be issued at a price ranging from HK$2.22 to HK$2.52, sources said.
About 90 percent of the issue is for placement and 10 percent is for public offer in Hong Kong, they said.

About 750 million yuan of the proceeds will be used to fund the phase I construction of a power plant in Zhang Jia Kou, in China's Hebei province, and another 923 million for the phase II development, said another analyst. The balance will be used to fund other power plant projects, he said.
Datang began its road show on February 25 and it plans a roadshow in the United States on March 3, and another in Europe on March 10, the sources said.
The public offering of shares in Hong Kong is expected to run from March 11 to 14. The price will be fixed on March 14 and dealing in shares will begin on March 21, they said.
Morgan Stanley is the lead manager of the issue.
H-shares are the shares of mainland Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong.
New World Infrastructure Ltd has said it will buy a 9.9 percent stake in Datang at the initial public offering price yet to be set for the H-share listing candidate.
